## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`refresh_fingerprints` overwrites fingerprints for files that are already tracked. That needs fixing because a hand-edited tracked file passed to the refresh command is silently re-approved, so verification can no longer detect the edit the PR body says it protects against.

## Changes
The pull request adds `refresh_fingerprints` and `register_new_files` to `app/integrity.py`, which update the JSON fingerprint manifest for given file names. It also adds `tests/test_integrity.py`, which covers both helpers.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Stop refresh_fingerprints overwriting tracked entries — If `names` includes an already-tracked file that was hand-edited, `entries[name] = fingerprint(root / name)` replaces its stored digest with the edited file's digest, and `verify` then returns True. This contradicts the PR body's "Existing fingerprints let verification detect hand-edited tracked files." — Running the refresh after adding new files, with any edited tracked file in the list, silently approves the tampering and defeats integrity verification. — Fix: Skip names already in `entries`, as `register_new_files` does at `app/integrity.py:24`, or make overwriting an explicit opt-in.

## Suggestions
- tests/test_integrity.py:12 — tests — Add an edited tracked file to the refresh test — `test_refresh_registers_new_files_and_keeps_unchanged_entries` passes only an unmodified `tracked.txt` to `refresh_fingerprints`, so it passes whether or not existing entries are overwritten. — The refresh test gives no protection against tampered tracked files being re-approved; `test_register_preserves_existing_fingerprints` covers this case only for the other helper. — Fix: Edit `tracked.txt` before the refresh call, as `test_register_preserves_existing_fingerprints` does, then assert the original digest is kept and `verify` returns False.
